config.notes: VU Melbourne course pages are bound to their INTERNATIONAL view, the path variant /courses/<slug>/international (rebound by hand 5 Oct; the plain address shows the domestic view: CSP/domestic full fee, domestic block start dates). The /international page is plain HTML (read by a direct fetch, no Firecrawl) and prints: key details "VU course code: X | CRICOS: X | Level of study: X Duration X Delivery mode X Fees Tuition: per semester AU$x Location X"; Fees section "Fees for full-time international student (2027): AU$x per semester. Fees for full-time international student (2026): AU$y per semester" (PER SEMESTER, not annual: no fee pattern; per-semester fees are an open decision); Start dates "<campus> Course starts 15 February 2027 Course starts 26 July 2027" (international dates). page_view cannot express a path variant (suffix only # ? &), so the view is reached by binding the /international address. VU Sydney/VU Brisbane pages are international views with "CRICOS code : x ... Intakes : 16 February, 27 July" and their own CRICOS codes; the intakes pattern takes either the Sydney/Brisbane line for the course's own code or each "Course starts <day> <Month>" (pick all). IELTS overall from "IELTS ... Overall score of x". Extras: Level of study, Duration, Delivery mode, Location, not admitting. Central English: https://www.vu.edu.au/sites/default/files/international-english-language-requirements.pdf (UG 6.0/6.0, PG 6.5/6.0, HE diploma 6.0/5.5, VET 5.5/5.0, named higher courses); key dates: https://www.vu.edu.au/current-students/your-course/timetables-calendars/academic-calendar (international intakes Semester 1 = February, Semester 2 = July) 5 Oct 15:22 checks: no exit awards with full-time years printed (VU Sydney business pages mention a Graduate Diploma as an exit point from a Masters, no years). Fees are per semester, never a whole-course total, so no fee_total. entry_requirement reads the academic entry requirement (Academic requirements / '...prerequisites for this course outlined below:' / Admission requirements International), shown for review only. The /international pages are bound by hand, so apply does not re-read them; they pick the pattern up only when re-read.
